what_its_for: Netarsudil is an eye drop used to lower pressure inside your eye. It is prescribed for a condition called glaucoma or high eye pressure (ocular hypertension). Lowering eye pressure helps protect your vision and prevents damage to your optic nerve.
how_to_take: Wash your hands thoroughly before using this medicine. Tilt your head back, pull down your lower eyelid to create a small pocket, and place one drop into that pocket. Close your eye gently for 1 to 2 minutes — do not blink hard or squeeze your eye shut. If you use other eye drops, wait at least 5 minutes between each medicine. To avoid contamination, do not let the dropper tip touch your eye, eyelid, or any other surface.
dosing: Use one drop in the affected eye (or eyes) once every evening at bedtime. Try to use it at the same time each night to get the most benefit. Do not use more drops than prescribed — using extra drops will not help more and may cause side effects.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, skip it and use your next dose the following evening at your regular time. Do not double up or use two doses at once to make up for the missed one.
storage: Store the bottle in the refrigerator between 36°F and 46°F (2°C to 8°C) before opening. After you open the bottle, you can keep it at room temperature between 36°F and 77°F (2°C to 25°C). Keep the bottle tightly closed when not in use. Throw away the bottle 6 weeks after you first open it, even if there is medicine left. Keep out of reach of children.
what_to_avoid: Do not wear contact lenses while using this eye drop. If your doctor approves contact lens use, wait at least 15 minutes after using the drop before putting your lenses in. Avoid touching the dropper tip to prevent contamination. Do not drive or operate heavy machinery right after using this drop until you are sure your vision is clear.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor if you notice: severe eye pain or increased discomfort, sudden changes in your vision, signs of eye infection such as increased redness, swelling, or discharge, a severe allergic reaction (rash, difficulty breathing, swelling of face or throat), or if your eye redness or irritation becomes very bothersome. Mild redness of the eye is common and usually not dangerous, but let your doctor know if it bothers you.
when_it_works: Netarsudil starts working within a few hours of your first dose. However, your doctor will check your eye pressure at follow-up visits to make sure it is working well for you. Keep using the drops even if you do not notice any symptoms — high eye pressure usually has no pain or obvious signs.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, as the safety of this medicine in these situations is not fully known. Children: This medicine is not typically recommended for children. Older adults: No special dose adjustment is needed for older adults, but always follow your doctor's instructions. Kidney or liver problems: No dose changes are generally needed, but inform your doctor about any other health conditions you have.
